facts.big: Could you tell me where…? / Turn left / It was repaired
facts.label: Revisão das direções
facts.sub: Use perguntas indiretas com ordem de afirmação (where the park is), imperativos para direções (turn left) e o passivo (was repaired, is used) para descrever lugares.

facts.label: Poderia me dizer…?
facts.sub: Use Could you tell me… ou Do you know… antes da pergunta: Do you know where the museum is? A ordem depois de where é de afirmação: where the museum is.

facts.label: Vire, vá
facts.sub: Use o verbo base para dar direções: Turn left. Cross the bridge. Walk along the water. No negativo, use don’t: Don’t wait for the bus.

compare.ask: Could you tell me where the park is?
compare.br: No Brasil, dizemos “você sabe onde é o parque?” sem mudar a ordem.
compare.tip: Diga: “Could you tell me where the park is?”
compare.us: Em inglês, a pergunta inicial usa do/could, mas a parte indireta volta à ordem normal: Do you know where the park is? Não use is antes do sujeito.

solo: Peça uma experiência pessoal do aluno com essa diferença.

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: Do you know where the park is? is an indirect question.
We say “Could you tell me where is the park?”
items.why: We say where the park is.

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

solo: Aluno responde e justifica; você mostra a pista.
group: Cada aluno decide sozinho, depois compare as respostas e peça uma justificativa.
Corrija pela pista do texto, não só dizendo “certo/errado”.
extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
answers: Do you know where the park is? is an indirect question. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)
We say “Could you tell me where is the park?” → Falso (We say where the park is.)
Turn left is an imperative. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)

pages.title: Lost in a new city · 1/3
paragraphs: It is a cloudy afternoon in Vancouver, and the streets are full. Dot and Ana stand at a crossroads with a paper map. They have walked for an hour, but nothing looks familiar. Dot holds the map upside down. Ana laughs and takes it from her. They need to find the way to the park.

“Ana, do you know where the museum is? I think we are lost.” says Dot. “I am not sure. Let me ask that man how to get to Stanley Park.” says Ana. “He says to go straight and turn left at the corner.” says Dot.

pages.title: Lost in a new city · 3/3
paragraphs: “I don’t know. Check your phone and tell me what it says.” says Ana. “It says that the park is open until nine. Come on, follow me!” says Dot. The two friends cross the old bridge. Ana puts the map in her bag. Dot sees the sign for the park. A little rain starts to fall. They walk faster and laugh together. Being lost can turn into a nice adventure.
